answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Ladder. Each identity must periodically answer a fresh challenge derived from its own interaction history; a clone sharing the same history produces an identical answer, a hollow copy detectable as non-divergent. Genuine agents accrue unique histories that signal authenticity over time. Copying another's full trajectory is the only pass, costing an attacker the compute to replay and maintain every fable in parallel, scaling linearly per clone — so mass cloning loses its cheapness.
